summary: In major defense space news, the U.S. Space Force selected 15 companies for a $981 million training range contract pool while outlining plans to achieve usable airborne target tracking capabilities by 2028. Internationally, Spain committed up to $2.3 billion to develop military communications infrastructure for Europe’s IRIS² constellation. Commercial sector growth saw satellite manufacturer K2 Space secure $500 million for expanding its commercial and defense capabilities, alongside federal interest in bypassing environmental regulations to streamline commercial launches and reentries. On the civil space front, NASA opened its new Flight Dynamics Research Facility at NASA Langley and advanced joint wind tunnel testing with SpaceX for the Starship rocket. NASA is also preparing to send two probes to lunar orbit to evaluate complex three-body trajectories and remains in the process of assessing flight opportunities for the Starliner-1 mission. In space science, Japan's space agency confirmed its probe achieved the closest-ever asteroid flyby, researchers used artificial intelligence to identify seven quasars that could explain supermassive black hole growth, and astronomers discovered the solar system's first three-headed asteroid featuring its own moon. Looking ahead, NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope remains on track for launch in late August.
